raw: {"analysis":"Response FMR correctly sequences the work so that code and documentation changes are ready before the irreversible registry change, and it explicitly handles the flaky network check, dual sign-off, orphaned jobs, and the read-only global-hooks file. Response MBC overcomplicates the plan with an excessive gate structure (G0-G10) and, critically, serializes the configuration and hooks work first before pipeline changes, which risks breaking webhook delivery for all 12 downstream services if the hooks are modified before the pipeline logic is ready to handle the new branch name. Response FMR's approach of landing pipeline and documentation changes to staging first, then performing the registry and hooks change as a serialized gate, is the safer and more operationally sound sequence.","verdict":"FMR"}
